surprises.description: Adjusted EPS growth was weaker than the preview’s +2.8% consensus expectation: EPS rose only about 1%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 3.3%, but its 20.5% margin was below the preview’s ~21.3% estimate, consistent with management saying sales-to-earnings conversion was below standards.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose only ~1% while adjusted EBITDA grew 3.3% to $1.4 billion at a 20.5% margin,” and management said conversion was “below standards.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $3.69” versus $3.59 a year earlier, or “+2.8%”; adjusted EBITDA margin was estimated at “~21.3%.”

surprises.description: Consolidated sales growth came in at high single digits, ahead of the preview’s +6.6% consensus growth expectation. The increase included mid-single-digit price/mix as well as low-single-digit volume and acquisition contributions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated sales grew high single-digits,” driven by “mid-single-digit price/mix and low single-digit contributions from acquisitions and volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net sales consensus was “$6.78B” versus $6,358.2M a year earlier, or “+6.6%.”

surprises.description: Consumer Brands Group adjusted gross margin fell 430 basis points, much worse than the preview’s picture of a margin that had held at 24.5% and Suvinil integration being an immaterial 2026 EPS tailwind. Suvinil dilution accounted for about 70% of the decline, with higher raw-material and supply-chain costs accounting for the rest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumer Brands Group adjusted gross margin fell 430 basis points,” with “approximately 70% attributable to Suvinil dilution” and the remainder to “higher raw material and supply chain costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CBG/Suvinil: adjusted margin held 24.5% in Q2 vs. 22.4% prior year”; integration was “guided as an immaterial EPS tailwind for 2026.”

surprises.description: Performance Coatings Group outperformed the preview’s modeled growth, with growth in every division and region; General Industrial grew mid-teens, while Packaging and Coil each grew low double digits. That breadth is stronger than the preview’s concern about Europe destocking and its +4.6% segment growth estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Performance Coatings Group beat expectations with growth in every division and region,” led by General Industrial “up mid-teens,” Packaging “up low double-digits,” and Coil “up low double-digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Performance Coatings sales growth of “+4.6%” and flagged “Europe destocking in PCG.”

surprises.description: Protective & Marine delivered mid-teens growth rather than the preview’s expected high-single-digit-or-better pace, and extended its streak to nine straight quarters. The preview had expected an eighth straight quarter at that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Protective & Marine posted mid-teens growth marking its ninth straight quarter of at least high single-digit growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “protective & marine (8th straight quarter of ≥HSD growth on data centers/semis).”

surprises.description: The preview identified September’s 8% Paint Stores Group increase as a risk to volume, including a bear case in which volume rolled over. Instead, the increase was tracking as planned, and the company reported volume growth in every quarter this year, though it did not provide a PSG-specific volume figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 8% Paint Stores Group price increase effective September 1 is tracking as planned”; the company also said volume growth was “achieved every quarter this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bear case needs volume to roll over in September,” and the preview highlighted possible “volume pushback from ‘fatigued’ contractors.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a quantified 2027 cost-savings plan of approximately $75 million, including $25 million from 2026 restructuring; the preview had discussed the need for a 2027 growth frame but did not anticipate this savings figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects approximately $75 million in 2027 cost savings (including $25 million from 2026 restructuring).”
